title: Nepal tour package from Delhi: flights and road
meta_description: Nepal tour packages from Delhi: 1 h 40 min flights to Kathmandu, road routes via Sonauli and Banbasa, documents for Indians and 3–6 night trip ideas.
summary: Delhi is the easiest Indian city for a Nepal trip: direct flights reach Kathmandu in about 1 hour 40 minutes, several times a day. A 3-night Kathmandu break starts around ₹14,000 per person plus flights, and a 6-night Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan tour from about ₹28,000. Indians need no visa, just a passport or Voter ID.
intro: Most Delhi travellers fly. With a morning flight you can be at Boudhanath by lunch, which makes a long-weekend Kathmandu break realistic and a 6-night circuit to Pokhara and Chitwan easy to fit into a week's leave. Popular trips from Delhi include the Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan loop, an Everest helicopter tour or mountain flight added to a city break, and the Pashupatinath–Muktinath pilgrimage. October–November and March–April are the busiest months, and fares rise sharply around Diwali, Christmas and long weekends, so book early.

Driving from Delhi is possible but long. The quickest road into central Nepal runs via the Yamuna and Agra–Lucknow expressways to Lucknow, then on to Gorakhpur and the Sonauli border, roughly 900 km and 14–16 hours, so most drivers break the trip in Lucknow. For the far west, the Banbasa crossing is closer, about 330–350 km via Bareilly and Pilibhit. A popular compromise is the overnight train to Gorakhpur, then a car to Lumbini and Pokhara, flying home from Kathmandu.
by_air: Air India, IndiGo and Nepal Airlines have operated direct Delhi–Kathmandu flights, with several departures a day and a flight time of about 1 hour 40 minutes into Tribhuvan International Airport (KTM). Morning departures give you a free afternoon in Kathmandu. Fares are lowest when booked four to six weeks ahead outside festival periods. There are no regular direct flights from Delhi to Bhairahawa (Gautam Buddha International); for Lumbini, fly to Kathmandu and connect on a 35-minute domestic flight. Schedules and airlines change, so check current status before you travel.
by_road: Two border crossings suit drivers from Delhi. Sonauli–Belahiya, via Lucknow and Gorakhpur, is about 900 km and 14–16 hours on expressways and national highways, and leads to Lumbini (30 km beyond), Pokhara (another 185 km) and Kathmandu (another 280 km). Banbasa–Mahendranagar, in Uttarakhand's Champawat district, is about 330–350 km and 7–8 hours via Moradabad, Bareilly and Pilibhit, but it leads into far-western Nepal, a long way from Kathmandu. Indian cars need a bhansar customs permit at the border.
by_rail: Many trains run overnight from Delhi to Gorakhpur in about 12–15 hours, making Gorakhpur the most practical railhead for Nepal. From there it is 95 km by road to Sonauli, or take a local train to Nautanwa, about 8 km from the border. Trains also run from Delhi towards Raxaul for Birgunj, and to Tanakpur near the Banbasa crossing.
documents: Indian citizens need no visa for Nepal. Adults must carry a valid Indian passport or Voter ID card, and airlines flying from Delhi accept only these two for adults. Children under 15 can travel with a passport or a photo ID showing age, such as a school ID, and 15–18 year olds with an identity certificate from their school principal. Aadhaar and PAN are not accepted as travel documents. OCI cardholders need a Nepal visa. Check current status before you travel.
tips: Book the earliest Delhi–Kathmandu flight so you reach your hotel by midday and can sightsee the same afternoon.
Ask for a window seat on the left side of the plane from Delhi for a chance of Himalayan views on clear mornings.
Carry Indian ₹100 notes and smaller, as rules on larger notes in Nepal have changed in recent years.
Add the Everest mountain flight to a Kathmandu break for close views of the highest peaks with no altitude risk.
Avoid Diwali week and the last week of December if price matters, as fares from Delhi rise sharply.

faqs.q: How much is a Nepal tour package from Delhi?
faqs.a: A 3-night Kathmandu package costs about ₹14,000–25,000 per person at 3-star, and a 6-night Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan tour about ₹28,000–45,000, twin sharing. Return flights from Delhi typically add ₹10,000–20,000 per person outside peak dates, more around Diwali and New Year. A 6-night trip at 5-star starts around ₹95,000 plus flights.

faqs.q: How long is the flight from Delhi to Kathmandu?
faqs.a: About 1 hour 40 minutes in the air. Add check-in time at Delhi and immigration at Kathmandu, which is quick for Indians showing a passport or Voter ID. Several direct flights usually operate daily. Kathmandu is 15 minutes ahead of Indian Standard Time, so set your watch forward when you land.

faqs.q: Can I go to Nepal from Delhi by road?
faqs.a: Yes. The usual route is Delhi–Lucknow–Gorakhpur–Sonauli, about 900 km and 14–16 hours, best split with a night in Lucknow or Gorakhpur. From the border, Lumbini is 30 km and Pokhara 185 km. Bring your car's papers for a bhansar permit, or leave the car in India and hire a Nepali vehicle at the border.

faqs.q: Is there a bus from Delhi to Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Direct bus services between Delhi and Kathmandu have run at various times, taking around 30 hours, but schedules have been irregular. Most travellers find the train to Gorakhpur plus a car or bus from Sonauli more reliable and comfortable. Check current status before you travel if you want a through bus.

faqs.q: What is the best Nepal itinerary from Delhi for 5 days?
faqs.a: Fly to Kathmandu and spend two nights seeing Pashupatinath, Boudhanath, Swayambhunath and Bhaktapur. Fly to Pokhara for two nights of boating, Sarangkot sunrise and perhaps paragliding, then fly back to Kathmandu for your flight home. Add the Everest mountain flight on your first full morning if the weather is clear.

faqs.q: Do I need a passport to go to Nepal from Delhi?
faqs.a: No, a passport is not essential. Indian citizens can fly from Delhi to Kathmandu with a valid Voter ID card instead. Aadhaar, PAN and driving licences are not accepted for adults. A passport is still the most convenient document, and you need one for the Kailash yatra or onward travel to Tibet. Check current status before you travel.

title: Nepal tour package from Mumbai: flights and prices
meta_description: Nepal tour packages from Mumbai: direct and one-stop flights to Kathmandu, train routes to Gorakhpur, documents for Indians and 5–8 night trip ideas.
summary: From Mumbai, a Nepal trip usually starts with a flight to Kathmandu of about 2.5–3 hours direct, or 4–6 hours via Delhi. We suggest at least 5–6 nights to make the journey worthwhile: Kathmandu, Pokhara and Chitwan from about ₹28,000 per person plus flights, with no visa needed for Indians.
intro: Mumbai travellers usually want the full picture in one trip: temples in Kathmandu, the lake and mountains of Pokhara and a jeep safari in Chitwan. Because the journey takes longer than from north India, we recommend 6–8 nights, often adding Nagarkot for sunrise or a Muktinath pilgrimage from Pokhara. Families like the Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan loop at 3-star, about ₹28,000–45,000 per person, while couples often choose 4-star honeymoon versions. Diwali, Christmas and the May school holidays are the busiest periods from Mumbai.

October–November suits most Mumbai travellers: the monsoon has cleared over the Himalaya and Dashain and Tihar are under way. April and May work for families despite haze over the mountains and heat in Chitwan. Trekkers from Mumbai's hiking clubs tend to choose Annapurna Base Camp or Everest Base Camp in October or April, flying to Kathmandu and taking a domestic flight to Pokhara or Lukla. Overland travel is rarely worth it from Mumbai, because the nearest main border crossing is about 1,700 km away.
by_air: IndiGo has operated direct Mumbai–Kathmandu flights of around 2.5–3 hours, but schedules vary by season. When there is no direct service, the usual option is one stop via Delhi, with Air India, IndiGo or Nepal Airlines on the Delhi–Kathmandu leg, taking about 4–6 hours in total. All flights land at Tribhuvan International Airport (KTM). There are no regular flights from Mumbai to Bhairahawa. Schedules and airlines change, so check current status before you travel.
by_road: Driving from Mumbai to Nepal means about 1,700 km to the Sonauli border through Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, roughly 30 hours at the wheel, best split over three days. From Sonauli, Lumbini is 30 km and Pokhara 185 km. It suits road-trip enthusiasts with time to spare rather than holidaymakers. Most Mumbai travellers who want an overland element fly to Delhi, Lucknow or Gorakhpur, or take the train to Gorakhpur, and drive the final stretch from there.
by_rail: Several long-distance trains run from Mumbai, mainly from Lokmanya Tilak Terminus, to Gorakhpur in about 28–34 hours, and some run to Raxaul for the Birgunj border. From Gorakhpur, Sonauli is 95 km by road. It is a long journey but useful for groups on a budget or pilgrims combining Nepal with Varanasi or Ayodhya.
documents: No visa is needed for Indian citizens. For the flight from Mumbai, adults must carry a valid Indian passport or Voter ID card; other IDs such as Aadhaar, PAN or a driving licence are not accepted as travel documents. Children travel most easily on their own passport; otherwise carry a school photo ID or birth certificate, and a principal's identity certificate for 15–18 year olds. OCI cardholders need a Nepal visa. Check current status before you travel.
tips: Plan at least six nights, since the journey from Mumbai takes most of a day each way.
Fly from Kathmandu to Pokhara rather than driving to save a full day on the road.
Book October and Diwali trips three months ahead, as Mumbai–Kathmandu flights fill early.
Pack a warm layer from November to February, when Kathmandu and Nagarkot mornings drop to 2–5 °C.
Carry Indian ₹100 notes and small change, as larger notes are not always accepted in Nepal.

faqs.q: Is there a direct flight from Mumbai to Kathmandu?
faqs.a: IndiGo has operated a direct Mumbai–Kathmandu service of about 2.5–3 hours, though not in every season. When it is not running, connect via Delhi, which takes about 4–6 hours including the layover. Check current status before you travel, and book early for October, Diwali and the May school holidays, when seats sell fast.

faqs.q: How much does a Nepal trip from Mumbai cost?
faqs.a: Land packages start around ₹28,000–45,000 per person for a 6-night Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan tour at 3-star, twin sharing. Return flights from Mumbai usually add ₹15,000–30,000 per person, more in peak periods. A 6-night trip at 4-star hotels with flights typically comes to ₹70,000–1,00,000 per person.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Nepal from Mumbai?
faqs.a: Six to eight nights. With travel taking most of a day each way, a shorter trip spends too much time in airports. Six nights covers Kathmandu, Pokhara and Chitwan at a comfortable pace; eight nights lets you add Nagarkot, Bandipur or a Muktinath pilgrimage. For a trek such as Annapurna Base Camp, plan 12–14 days.

faqs.q: Can I take a train from Mumbai to Nepal?
faqs.a: There is no train into Nepal from Mumbai, but trains run from Lokmanya Tilak Terminus to Gorakhpur in about 28–34 hours. From Gorakhpur, drive 95 km to the Sonauli border and continue to Lumbini or Pokhara. It is cheaper than flying but takes far longer, so it suits groups and pilgrims with time.

faqs.q: Which is the best time to visit Nepal from Mumbai?
faqs.a: October to November is best for clear Himalayan views and festivals, and fits the Diwali break. March to April is also good. May suits Mumbai's school holidays, though it is hot in Chitwan and hazy in the mountains. June to September is monsoon in Nepal too, with cloud and flight delays.

faqs.q: Do Mumbai residents need a visa for Nepal?
faqs.a: No. Indian citizens, wherever they live in India, need no visa for Nepal. Carry a valid Indian passport or Voter ID card for the flight. Foreign nationals living in Mumbai, including OCI cardholders, need a Nepal visa, which most nationalities can obtain on arrival at Kathmandu airport. Check current status before you travel.

title: Nepal tour package from Kolkata: flights and road
meta_description: Nepal tour packages from Kolkata: direct flights to Kathmandu, train to New Jalpaiguri for Kakarbhitta, the Raxaul crossing, documents and trip ideas.
summary: Kolkata has two good ways into Nepal: a direct flight of about 1.5 hours to Kathmandu, or an overnight train to New Jalpaiguri and a short drive to the Kakarbhitta border for eastern Nepal. A 6-night Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan tour costs about ₹28,000–45,000 per person plus travel, and Indians need no visa.
intro: Bengali travellers have long favoured Nepal for the Puja holidays, and October is the busiest month from Kolkata, often coinciding with Dashain in Nepal. Popular choices include Kathmandu with Pokhara and Chitwan, a Pashupatinath and Manakamana pilgrimage, and the Everest mountain flight. Eastern Nepal is close to Kolkata via Siliguri: the tea gardens of Ilam, the hill temple of Pathibhara and the Kanchenjunga region are all reached from the Kakarbhitta border, and combine well with a few days in Darjeeling.

For a first visit, we suggest flying to Kathmandu and spending 6–7 nights in the Kathmandu Valley, Pokhara and Chitwan. Travellers who have already seen Darjeeling or Sikkim often enjoy the overland route into Ilam, with its rolling tea estates, before flying from Bhadrapur to Kathmandu. Winter, from December to February, brings clear views and lower prices, while April suits families during school holidays. Book Puja and Diwali trips three to four months ahead, as flights and hotels fill early.
by_air: IndiGo has operated direct Kolkata–Kathmandu flights of about 1 hour 30 minutes into Tribhuvan International Airport (KTM), and other carriers have served the route at times. One-stop options via Delhi take much longer. For eastern Nepal, you can also fly Kathmandu–Bhadrapur or Kathmandu–Biratnagar on domestic flights of under an hour. There are no regular flights from Kolkata to Bhairahawa. Schedules and airlines change, so check current status before you travel.
by_road: The nearest crossing is Panitanki–Kakarbhitta, about 35 km from Siliguri and roughly 570 km from Kolkata by road, 11–13 hours. From Kakarbhitta, Ilam is about 3 hours away and Bhadrapur airport under an hour. Jogbani–Biratnagar, about 530 km from Kolkata via Purnia, is better for Biratnagar and Koshi Tappu. For central Nepal, Raxaul–Birgunj is roughly 750 km from Kolkata, followed by about 270 km and 7–9 hours to Kathmandu.
by_rail: Overnight trains from Kolkata to New Jalpaiguri (NJP) take about 10–12 hours, and NJP is about 35 km and an hour by road from the Kakarbhitta border. Trains also run from Kolkata to Jogbani for Biratnagar, and the Mithila Express runs overnight from Howrah to Raxaul for Birgunj.
documents: Indian citizens need no visa for Nepal and can enter at Kakarbhitta, Jogbani or by air with a valid passport or Voter ID card. Children under 15 should carry a passport or photo ID showing age, and 15–18 year olds without a passport an identity certificate from their school principal. Aadhaar is not accepted as a travel document for adults. Foreign companions need a Nepal visa. Check current status before you travel.
tips: Book Durga Puja and Diwali trips early, as Kolkata–Kathmandu flights and Kathmandu hotels fill fast in October.
Combine Darjeeling with Ilam by crossing at Kakarbhitta, about an hour from Siliguri.
Fly Bhadrapur–Kathmandu after visiting Ilam to avoid a 14–16 hour drive west.
Avoid the overland route to Ilam from June to September, when monsoon landslides affect hill roads.
Carry ₹100 notes and smaller, as larger Indian notes are not always accepted in Nepal.

faqs.q: How much is a Nepal tour package from Kolkata?
faqs.a: A 6-night Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan package costs about ₹28,000–45,000 per person at 3-star, twin sharing, plus return flights from Kolkata, which typically add ₹10,000–20,000 outside the Puja and Diwali peak. An eastern Nepal trip to Ilam by road from Siliguri avoids international flights entirely and usually costs less overall.

faqs.q: How do I go to Nepal from Kolkata by train?
faqs.a: Take an overnight train from Kolkata to New Jalpaiguri, about 10–12 hours, then drive about an hour to the Panitanki–Kakarbhitta border. For central Nepal, take the Mithila Express from Howrah to Raxaul and cross to Birgunj, then drive to Chitwan in 3–4 hours or Kathmandu in 7–9 hours. Both routes avoid flying.

faqs.q: What is the distance from Siliguri to the Nepal border?
faqs.a: Siliguri to the Panitanki–Kakarbhitta border is about 35 km, roughly an hour by road. New Jalpaiguri station and Bagdogra airport are a similar distance away. From Kakarbhitta, the tea town of Ilam is about 3 hours, and Bhadrapur airport, with flights to Kathmandu, is under an hour away.

faqs.q: Can I combine Darjeeling and Nepal in one trip?
faqs.a: Yes, it is a natural pairing. Spend two or three nights in Darjeeling, drive down to Siliguri and cross at Kakarbhitta to Ilam for tea gardens and views towards Kanchenjunga. From there, fly Bhadrapur to Kathmandu for the Kathmandu Valley and Pokhara. Allow 8–10 nights for the full route.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Nepal from Kolkata?
faqs.a: October to November is the classic time, matching Durga Puja and Diwali breaks with clear mountain views, though it is the busiest season. December to February is cold but sunny and cheaper. March and April suit school holidays, with rhododendrons in the eastern hills. Avoid June to September for the overland route because of landslides.

faqs.q: Do I need a passport to enter Nepal at Kakarbhitta?
faqs.a: No. Indian citizens can enter at Kakarbhitta with a valid Voter ID card instead of a passport, and no visa is required. Carry the original, as photocopies may not be accepted. Children should carry photo ID showing their age. Foreign nationals need a visa, which is issued at Kakarbhitta for most nationalities. Check current status before you travel.

title: Nepal tour package from Bengaluru: flights and treks
meta_description: Nepal tour packages from Bengaluru: flights to Kathmandu via Delhi or Kolkata, trek and tour ideas, documents for Indians and the best months to go.
summary: From Bengaluru, Kathmandu is about 3 hours by direct flight when services run, or 5–7 hours via Delhi or Kolkata. We recommend 6–8 nights for Kathmandu, Pokhara and Chitwan from about ₹28,000 per person plus flights, or 10–14 days for Annapurna and Everest treks. Indians need no visa.
intro: Bengaluru has a large trekking community, and Poon Hill, Annapurna Base Camp and Everest Base Camp are natural next steps for weekend hikers used to the Western Ghats. October–November and April–May give the best trekking weather. For non-trekkers, the Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan loop over six or seven nights covers temples, lakes and wildlife, and adding a Pokhara paragliding flight or the Everest mountain flight is common. Kathmandu's cafes and Pokhara's lakeside make easy bases for remote workers adding a few days to a holiday.

Because the journey from South India takes most of a day, short trips are hard to justify; plan at least six nights for a tour or two weeks for a trek. Many Bengaluru travellers fly to Kathmandu, spend two nights in the valley, then fly to Pokhara as a base for Poon Hill or Annapurna. South Indian Vaishnava pilgrims often add Muktinath, counted among the 108 Divya Desams, to a Pokhara stay. Book October trips three months ahead, as Dashain and Diwali fill flights.
by_air: Direct flights between Bengaluru and Kathmandu have operated at times, taking about 3 hours, but they are not always on the schedule. The dependable option is one stop via Delhi or Kolkata, with a total journey of about 5–7 hours, landing at Tribhuvan International Airport (KTM). Air India and IndiGo connect through Delhi, and IndiGo also through Kolkata. For Pokhara, change in Kathmandu to a 25-minute domestic flight. Schedules and airlines change, so check current status before you travel.
by_road: Road travel from Bengaluru to Nepal is impractical for most holidays: the Sonauli border is roughly 2,100–2,300 km away, about 40 hours of driving. If you want an overland element, fly to Lucknow, Varanasi or Gorakhpur, then drive to Sonauli (95 km from Gorakhpur, about 2–2.5 hours) and continue to Lumbini, 30 km beyond the border, and Pokhara, 185 km beyond it. Return by air from Kathmandu to save time.
by_rail: Long-distance trains run from Bengaluru to Gorakhpur in roughly 40–45 hours, and Gorakhpur is 95 km by road from the Sonauli border. The journey suits pilgrim groups with plenty of time, but most travellers from Bengaluru fly at least as far as north India.
documents: Indian citizens need no visa for Nepal. Adults flying from Bengaluru must carry a valid Indian passport or Voter ID card; Aadhaar, PAN and driving licences are not accepted as travel documents. For children, a passport is simplest; otherwise carry a photo ID showing age, and a school principal's certificate for 15–18 year olds. For treks into restricted areas such as Manaslu, bring your passport. Check current status before you travel.
tips: Book a connection with at least two hours in Delhi or Kolkata, as bags may need re-checking on separate tickets.
Break in your trekking boots on Nandi Hills or Savandurga before an Annapurna or Everest trek.
Pack warm layers, as Kathmandu winter mornings drop to around 2–3 °C, far colder than Bengaluru.
Use Pokhara as your base for Poon Hill or Annapurna Base Camp, the best-value treks in a 10–12 day trip.
Carry ₹100 notes and smaller, as larger Indian notes are not always accepted in Nepal.

faqs.q: Is there a direct flight from Bengaluru to Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Direct Bengaluru–Kathmandu flights have run at times, taking about 3 hours, but not consistently. Most travellers connect via Delhi or Kolkata, with a total journey of 5–7 hours. Book a single ticket through to Kathmandu if possible, so bags are checked through to your destination. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How much does a Nepal trip from Bengaluru cost?
faqs.a: A 6-night Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan tour costs about ₹28,000–45,000 per person at 3-star, twin sharing. Return flights from Bengaluru usually add ₹18,000–35,000 per person depending on season and routing. An Annapurna Base Camp trek costs roughly US$750–1,100 for 10–12 days from Kathmandu, plus your flights.

faqs.q: Which Nepal trek is best for Bengaluru trekkers?
faqs.a: For a first Himalayan trek, Poon Hill (4–5 days, 3,210 m) or Annapurna Base Camp (10–12 days, 4,130 m) are good choices, both from Pokhara. Trekkers with Himalayan experience in Uttarakhand or Himachal often choose Everest Base Camp, 12–14 days with Kala Patthar at 5,644 m. All are best in October–November or March–May.

faqs.q: How many days are needed for Nepal from Bengaluru?
faqs.a: At least six nights for a tour, as travel takes most of a day each way. Six nights covers Kathmandu, Pokhara and Chitwan; eight nights adds Nagarkot or a Muktinath trip. For treks, plan 10–12 days for Annapurna Base Camp and 14–16 days for Everest Base Camp, including a buffer day for flights.

faqs.q: When should I visit Nepal from Bengaluru?
faqs.a: October and November are best for clear mountain views and trekking, though busy. March to May is the second season, with rhododendrons and warmer weather. December to February is cold but clear, good for Kathmandu, Pokhara and Chitwan. Avoid June to September for treks, as monsoon cloud hides the mountains and delays flights.

faqs.q: Can South Indian pilgrims visit Muktinath from Pokhara?
faqs.a: Yes. Muktinath, at 3,710 m, is among the 108 Divya Desams and a major pilgrimage for Sri Vaishnava devotees. From Pokhara, travel by jeep in 8–10 hours, by a 20-minute flight to Jomsom plus a jeep, or by helicopter in about 25 minutes. South Indian vegetarian food is limited near the temple, so carry snacks.

title: Nepal tour package from Chennai: flights and yatras
meta_description: Nepal tour packages from Chennai: flights via Delhi, Kolkata or Bengaluru, Muktinath and Pashupatinath yatras, documents for Indians and best months.
summary: From Chennai, Kathmandu is usually reached by a one-stop flight of 5–7 hours via Delhi, Kolkata or Bengaluru. Many Chennai travellers combine Pashupatinath with Muktinath, one of the 108 Divya Desams, over 6–8 nights from about ₹30,000–45,000 per person by road, plus flights. Indians need no visa, only a passport or Voter ID.
intro: Muktinath draws many Tamil pilgrims, as it is revered as Thiru Saligramam, one of the 108 Divya Desams praised by the Alvars. A typical yatra from Chennai flies to Kathmandu for darshan at Pashupatinath and Budhanilkantha, continues to Pokhara, and reaches Muktinath (3,710 m) by jeep, Jomsom flight or helicopter. The Kali Gandaki, source of the sacred saligrama stones, is part of the story, and pilgrims often look for saligrams in Jomsom or along the river near Kagbeni.

Travellers from Chennai who are not on a yatra usually choose a 6–7 night Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan tour, adding Nagarkot sunrise or paragliding in Pokhara. Because the journey takes most of a day, we suggest at least six nights. October to November is busiest; December to February offers clear skies but cold mornings that surprise many Chennai visitors, close to freezing at Nagarkot and well below at Muktinath. Hotels in Kathmandu and Pokhara can arrange South Indian vegetarian meals with notice; menus are simpler higher up.
by_air: There are no regular direct flights from Chennai to Kathmandu. Most travellers fly one stop via Delhi, Kolkata or Bengaluru with IndiGo or Air India, taking about 5–7 hours including the connection, and land at Tribhuvan International Airport (KTM). For Muktinath, connect in Kathmandu to Pokhara (25 minutes), then fly to Jomsom (about 20 minutes) or take a helicopter. Book through tickets so bags are checked to Kathmandu. Schedules and airlines change, so check current status before you travel.
by_road: Driving from Chennai is impractical: the Sonauli border is roughly 2,200 km away, two to three days of driving. Pilgrims who prefer an overland approach usually fly or take the train to Varanasi or Gorakhpur, then drive to the Sonauli border, which is 95 km and 2–2.5 hours from Gorakhpur, and on to Pokhara, 185 km and 7–8 hours beyond, the base for Muktinath. From Varanasi, Sonauli is about 300–320 km and 7–8 hours.
by_rail: Trains from Chennai to Gorakhpur take roughly 38–42 hours, and Gorakhpur is 95 km by road from the Sonauli border. Pilgrims sometimes combine the rail journey with Varanasi and Ayodhya before crossing into Nepal. It suits groups with two weeks or more; most travellers from Chennai fly.
documents: Indian citizens need no visa for Nepal. Adults flying from Chennai must show a valid Indian passport or Voter ID card; Aadhaar, PAN and driving licences are not accepted for travel to Nepal. Senior citizens over 65 have been allowed other photo IDs showing age at land borders, but airlines expect a passport or Voter ID. Children should carry a passport or photo ID showing age. Check current status before you travel.
tips: Choose a Jomsom flight or helicopter for Muktinath if travelling with seniors, rather than the 8–10 hour jeep road.
Pack thermals, gloves and a warm cap, as Muktinath mornings are near or below freezing from November to March.
Ask hotels in advance for South Indian vegetarian meals, and carry ready-to-eat snacks for Mustang.
Allow a buffer day in Pokhara, as Jomsom flights are often delayed by wind.
Carry ₹100 notes and smaller, as larger Indian notes are not always accepted in Nepal.

faqs.q: How do I travel from Chennai to Muktinath?
faqs.a: Fly from Chennai to Kathmandu via Delhi, Kolkata or Bengaluru, then take a 25-minute flight to Pokhara. From Pokhara, reach Muktinath by a 20-minute flight to Jomsom and a 1.5-hour jeep ride, by helicopter in about 25 minutes, or by jeep in 8–10 hours. A full yatra usually takes 6–8 nights from Chennai.

faqs.q: What is the cost of a Muktinath yatra from Chennai?
faqs.a: A 6–7 night Kathmandu–Pokhara–Muktinath yatra by road and jeep usually costs ₹30,000–45,000 per person at 3-star, twin sharing, starting in Kathmandu. Return flights from Chennai typically add ₹18,000–35,000. Pokhara–Jomsom flights add roughly ₹12,000–20,000, and a Muktinath helicopter from Pokhara costs ₹45,000–65,000 per seat.

faqs.q: Is Muktinath a Divya Desam?
faqs.a: Yes. Muktinath is revered as Thiru Saligramam, one of the 108 Divya Desams of the Sri Vaishnava tradition, praised by the Alvars. It is also sacred to Shiva devotees and to Buddhists, who call it Chumig Gyatsa. Pilgrims bathe under the 108 water spouts and in the two kunds before darshan of the Vishnu image.

faqs.q: Is there a direct flight from Chennai to Kathmandu?
faqs.a: No regular direct flight operates on this route. Connect through Delhi, Kolkata or Bengaluru on IndiGo or Air India, with a total travel time of about 5–7 hours. faqs.q: Is there a train from Bihar to Nepal?
faqs.a: Yes. A cross-border passenger railway runs from Jaynagar in Bihar to Janakpur and Kurtha in Nepal, with services that began in 2022. Indian citizens can travel with a passport or Voter ID. For Birgunj, trains run to Raxaul Junction, and you cross the border by road. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How do I go from Patna to Kathmandu?
faqs.a: By road, drive to Raxaul in 5–6 hours, cross to Birgunj and continue to Kathmandu via Hetauda in 7–9 hours, ideally with a night in Chitwan. Faster still, fly from Simara near Birgunj to Kathmandu in about 20 minutes. Flights from Patna connect via Delhi or Kolkata, which takes 4–6 hours.

faqs.q: How far is Janakpur from Patna?
faqs.a: Janakpur is roughly 220–250 km from Patna, about 6–7 hours, via Darbhanga and the Jaynagar or Bhitthamore crossings. You can also take a train to Jaynagar and the cross-border train to Janakpur. The Janaki Mandir, Ram Mandir and Dhanush Sagar are the main sights, and Vivah Panchami is the busiest time.

faqs.q: Can I take my car from Patna into Nepal?
faqs.a: Yes. At the Birgunj customs office, show your car's registration certificate, insurance, driving licence and ID to get a bhansar permit, paying a daily fee. Roads from Birgunj to Chitwan are flat, but the drive to Kathmandu climbs steep hill roads, so it suits experienced drivers only. Check current status before you travel.

title: Nepal tour package from Varanasi by air and road
meta_description: Nepal tour packages from Varanasi: Buddha Air flights to Kathmandu, road via Gorakhpur and Sonauli, Lumbini and Pashupatinath trips, documents, tips.
summary: Varanasi links to Nepal by air and road. Buddha Air has flown Varanasi–Kathmandu in about an hour, and the Sonauli border is about 300–320 km, 7–8 hours, via Gorakhpur. Pilgrims often pair Kashi Vishwanath with Pashupatinath, and Buddhists link Sarnath with Lumbini. Indians need no visa, just a passport or Voter ID.
intro: Varanasi travellers often see Nepal as the second half of a pilgrimage. Hindu pilgrims link Kashi Vishwanath with Pashupatinath in Kathmandu, and many add Manakamana and Muktinath. Buddhist groups travel from Sarnath to Kushinagar and on to Lumbini, the Buddha's birthplace, crossing at Sonauli. Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan tours also work well from Varanasi, especially by flying to Kathmandu and returning overland via Lumbini and Sonauli, which avoids retracing your route and adds the Buddha's birthplace on the way home.

A typical 5–6 night trip flies from Varanasi to Kathmandu for two nights, drives or flies to Pokhara for two nights, then heads south to Lumbini for a night before crossing at Sonauli and returning to Varanasi by road, or by train from Gorakhpur. At 3-star, the Nepal portion costs about ₹28,000–45,000 per person, twin sharing. October to March is the most comfortable season; April to June is very hot in Lumbini and the Terai, often above 38 °C.
by_air: Buddha Air has operated direct Varanasi–Kathmandu flights of about an hour, landing at Tribhuvan International Airport (KTM), though frequency varies by season. Otherwise, connect via Delhi, where Air India, IndiGo and Nepal Airlines fly to Kathmandu, for a total of about 4–5 hours. Travellers heading only to Lumbini can drive to Sonauli instead and skip flying altogether. Schedules and airlines change, so check current status before you travel.
by_road: Sonauli–Belahiya is the natural crossing, about 300–320 km from Varanasi via Gorakhpur, roughly 7–8 hours. From the border, Lumbini is 30 km, Pokhara 185 km and Kathmandu 280 km. Buddhist circuit groups often drive Varanasi–Kushinagar, about 250 km and 6–7 hours, then continue to Sonauli, about 150 km via Gorakhpur, the next day. Raxaul–Birgunj, roughly 400 km away, is an option for Chitwan.
by_rail: Frequent trains link Varanasi with Gorakhpur in about 5–7 hours, and Gorakhpur is 95 km from the Sonauli border by road. Local trains run on from Gorakhpur to Nautanwa, about 8 km from the crossing. Trains to Raxaul via Chhapra and Muzaffarpur are also possible for the Birgunj border.
documents: Indian citizens need no visa for Nepal. For the flight to Kathmandu or the Sonauli crossing, adults must carry a valid Indian passport or Voter ID card; Aadhaar and PAN are not accepted. Children under 15 should carry photo ID showing age, and 15–18 year olds without a passport a school principal's certificate. Foreign Buddhist pilgrims travelling with Indian groups need a Nepal visa, available at Sonauli. Check current status before you travel.
tips: Fly from Varanasi to Kathmandu and return overland via Lumbini and Sonauli to avoid retracing your route.
Visit Lumbini between October and March, as April to June temperatures often exceed 38 °C.
Link Sarnath, Kushinagar and Lumbini over three days for a compact Buddhist circuit.
Go for Pashupatinath darshan early in the morning to avoid queues, especially on Mondays.
Carry ₹100 notes and smaller, as larger Indian notes are not always accepted in Nepal.

faqs.q: Is there a direct flight from Varanasi to Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Buddha Air has operated direct Varanasi–Kathmandu flights of about an hour, giving Varanasi one of the few direct links to Nepal outside India's big metros. Frequency changes by season, so check current status before you travel. If no flight suits, connect via Delhi or travel overland through Gorakhpur and Sonauli.

faqs.q: What is the distance from Varanasi to Lumbini?
faqs.a: Varanasi to Lumbini is about 330–350 km by road via Gorakhpur and the Sonauli border, roughly 8–9 hours including border formalities. Buddhist circuit groups often break the journey at Kushinagar. Alternatively, take a train to Gorakhpur in 5–7 hours and drive the remaining 125 km or so to Lumbini.

faqs.q: How much is a Nepal tour package from Varanasi?
faqs.a: A 5–6 night Kathmandu–Pokhara–Lumbini tour costs about ₹28,000–45,000 per person at 3-star, twin sharing, excluding the flight or road journey from Varanasi. A 2-night Lumbini trip by road from Varanasi costs much less. A Pashupatinath–Muktinath yatra by road from Kathmandu costs ₹30,000–45,000.

faqs.q: Can I combine Kashi Vishwanath and Pashupatinath in one trip?
faqs.a: Yes, and many pilgrims do. Have darshan at Kashi Vishwanath, then fly to Kathmandu for Pashupatinath, or drive via Gorakhpur and Sonauli to include Lumbini and Pokhara. Hindus can enter the main Pashupatinath courtyard, and the evening aarti on the Bagmati ghats is a fitting end to the day.

faqs.q: What is the best Buddhist circuit route from Varanasi to Nepal?
faqs.a: Start at Sarnath near Varanasi, drive to Kushinagar in 6–7 hours, continue via Gorakhpur to Sonauli and Lumbini in 4–5 hours, and spend two nights in Lumbini to see Tilaurakot and Ramagrama. From there, return to India or continue to Kathmandu for Boudhanath and Swayambhunath. Bodh Gaya can be added at the start.

faqs.q: Do I need a passport to fly from Varanasi to Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Indian citizens can fly with a valid Voter ID card instead of a passport. Aadhaar, PAN and driving licences are not accepted for adults. Children should carry a passport or photo ID showing age. Check current status before you travel, as airline and immigration rules can change.

title: Nepal tour package from Gorakhpur via Sonauli
meta_description: Nepal tour packages from Gorakhpur: 95 km to the Sonauli border, Lumbini, Pokhara and Muktinath by road, flights from Bhairahawa, documents and tips.
summary: Gorakhpur is the closest major city to Nepal's main tourist crossing: Sonauli is 95 km away, about 2–2.5 hours by road. From there, Lumbini is 30 km, Pokhara 185 km and Kathmandu 280 km. A 4-night Lumbini–Pokhara trip suits families, and Indians need no visa, just a passport or Voter ID.
intro: Gorakhpur sits at the doorstep of Nepal, and most of its travellers go by road. A popular 4–5 night trip crosses at Sonauli, visits Lumbini for the Maya Devi Temple and monasteries, then drives the Siddhartha Highway through Tansen to Pokhara for Phewa Lake and Sarangkot sunrise. Pilgrims extend to Muktinath from Pokhara by jeep, flight or helicopter. A 4–5 night road trip at 3-star with a private Nepali car usually costs about ₹22,000–35,000 per person, twin sharing.

Gorakhpur is also the main railhead for travellers from across India heading to Nepal, so many trips begin at its station. Kathmandu is about 8–10 hours from the border by road, or 35 minutes by air from Gautam Buddha International Airport at Bhairahawa, a short drive from Sonauli. Chitwan, about 4–5 hours from the border via Butwal and Narayangadh, adds a jeep safari. October to March is the best season; April to June is hot in Lumbini, and July–August brings landslides on the Siddhartha Highway.
by_air: Gorakhpur airport has domestic flights within India only, with no regular flights to Kathmandu. The practical option is to drive 95 km to Sonauli and fly from Gautam Buddha International Airport at Bhairahawa, a short drive from the border, to Kathmandu in about 35 minutes with Nepali domestic airlines such as Buddha Air or Yeti Airlines. Alternatively, fly from Gorakhpur to Delhi and connect to Kathmandu. Schedules change, so check current status before you travel.
by_road: Sonauli–Belahiya is 95 km from Gorakhpur via Pharenda and Nautanwa, about 2–2.5 hours. From Belahiya, Bhairahawa is about 4 km, Lumbini about 30 km (45 minutes), Pokhara about 185 km via Butwal and Tansen on the Siddhartha Highway (7–8 hours), and Kathmandu about 280 km via Narayangadh and Mugling (8–10 hours). Indian cars need a bhansar customs permit at the Belahiya customs office, charged per day.
by_rail: Gorakhpur Junction is one of north India's major railway stations, with direct trains from Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and southern cities. For the border, local trains run from Gorakhpur to Nautanwa in about 2–3 hours, and Nautanwa is about 8 km from Sonauli by auto or taxi. Most travellers find a taxi from Gorakhpur station quicker.
documents: Indian citizens need no visa for Nepal. At Sonauli, carry a valid Indian passport or Voter ID card; there is no stamp for Indians, but officials may check. Children under 15 should carry photo ID showing age, and 15–18 year olds without a passport a school principal's identity certificate. Airlines on the Bhairahawa–Kathmandu flight also ask for these documents. Foreign nationals need a Nepal visa, available at the border. Check current status before you travel.
tips: Leave Gorakhpur by 7 am to clear Sonauli before the midday rush of trucks and buses.
Change money at banks or licensed exchange counters in Bhairahawa rather than with street changers.
Spend a night in Lumbini or Tansen to break the long drive to Pokhara.
Fly Bhairahawa–Kathmandu to save a full day if your trip includes both Pokhara and Kathmandu.
Carry ₹100 notes and smaller, as larger Indian notes are not always accepted in Nepal.

faqs.q: How far is Nepal from Gorakhpur?
faqs.a: The Sonauli–Belahiya border is 95 km from Gorakhpur, about 2–2.5 hours by road. Bhairahawa is just across the border, Lumbini about 30 km further, Pokhara about 185 km and Kathmandu about 280 km beyond the border. A taxi from Gorakhpur station to Sonauli is the quickest way to reach the crossing.

faqs.q: How much is a Nepal tour package from Gorakhpur?
faqs.a: A 4–5 night Lumbini–Pokhara road trip from the Sonauli border costs about ₹22,000–35,000 per person at 3-star with a private Nepali car, twin sharing. A 6-night circuit adding Kathmandu and Chitwan costs ₹28,000–45,000. A Muktinath extension from Pokhara adds roughly ₹12,000–20,000 by jeep or Jomsom flight, or ₹45,000–65,000 by helicopter.

faqs.q: How do I go from Gorakhpur to Pokhara?
faqs.a: Drive 95 km to Sonauli in 2–2.5 hours, cross the border at Belahiya, then take the Siddhartha Highway via Butwal and Tansen to Pokhara, about 185 km and 7–8 hours. The road is winding, so many travellers stop overnight in Lumbini or Tansen. Tourist buses also run from Belahiya to Pokhara.

faqs.q: Can I fly from Gorakhpur to Kathmandu?
faqs.a: There are no regular direct flights. The fastest route is to drive to Sonauli and fly from Gautam Buddha International Airport at Bhairahawa to Kathmandu in about 35 minutes. You can also fly Gorakhpur–Delhi–Kathmandu, but that takes considerably longer. Check current status before you travel, as schedules change.

faqs.q: What documents do I need at the Sonauli border?
faqs.a: Indian citizens need a valid Indian passport or Voter ID card; no visa or stamp is required. Children should carry photo ID showing age. If you drive your own car, bring the registration certificate, insurance and driving licence for the bhansar permit. Foreign nationals need a passport and a Nepal visa, available at the border.

faqs.q: What is the best short trip from Gorakhpur to Nepal?
faqs.a: A 3-night trip works well: one night in Lumbini for the Maya Devi Temple and monastic zone, then two nights in Pokhara for Phewa Lake, Sarangkot sunrise and the caves and waterfalls around the city. For a single night, Lumbini alone is easy, about 3–4 hours from Gorakhpur including the border.
